etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English rim, rym, rime, from Old English rima (“rim, edge, border, bank, coast”), from Proto-Germanic *rimô, *rembô (“edge, border”), from Proto-Indo-European *rem-, *remə- (“to rest, support, be based”). Cognate with Saterland Frisian Rim (“plank, wooden cross, trellis”), Old Saxon rimi (“edge; border; trim”), Icelandic rimi (“a strip of land”).

definitions.definition: An edge around something, especially when circular.

quote.citation: 2007 September 25, Bungie, Halo 3, spoken by Master Chief (Steve Downes), Microsoft Game Studios, Xbox 360, level/area: The Ark:
quote.text: That's... our galaxy. We're beyond the rim.

quote.citation: 2010, Rochelle Magee, No Witnesses: A Perilous Journey, page 36:
quote.text: About an hour later, she noticed an all black Phantom with tints and chrome rims riding slowly through the car lot.
COPY READER — Journeyman, experienced makeup, now slot man on metropolitan midwest daily. Will travel for good rim job on large paper.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To follow the contours, possibly creating a circuit.
(transitive or intransitive, of a ball) To roll around a rim.

etymologies.etymologyHTML: From a variation of ream.

etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English rim, rym, ryme, reme, from Old English rēoma (“membrane, ligament”), from Proto-West Germanic *reumō.
